edges.description: Reduced UGDH activity decreases production of UDP-glucuronic acid from UDP-glucose.
Disrupted glycan-dependent extracellular matrix production impairs brain development and neuronal network function.

nodes.description: The central nervous system phenotype includes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, severe developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and motor disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in UDP-Glucose 6-Dehydrogenase cause recessive developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: All 30 patients carrying biallelic mutations in UGDH presented with a common core phenotype consisting of marked developmental delay, epilepsy, mild dysmorphism, and motor disorder with axial hypotonia

nodes.description: UDP-glucuronic acid shortage impairs production of glycosaminoglycan-rich extracellular matrix components, including proteoglycans and glycolipids that are important in human brain development.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in UDP-Glucose 6-Dehydrogenase cause recessive developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Our study defines UGDH as a key player for the production of extracellular matrix components that are essential for human brain development.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in UDP-Glucose 6-Dehydrogenase cause recessive developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report an allelic series of germline recessive mutations in UGDH in 36 cases from 25 families presenting with epileptic encephalopathy with developmental delay and hypotonia.

nodes.description: Pathogenic biallelic UGDH variants reduce the stability, oligomerization, or catalytic activity of UDP-glucose 6-dehydrogenase.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function mutations in UDP-Glucose 6-Dehydrogenase cause recessive developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with being loss-of-function alleles, we show using patients' primary fibroblasts and biochemical assays, that these mutations either impair UGDH stability, oligomerization, or enzymatic activity.
